name: Reelaiah
overview: Reelaiah was a male figure who returned to Judah following the Babylonian captivity, as recorded in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah. His return signifies participation in the restoration of the Jewish community after exile. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Reelaiah appears in Ezra 2:2 without a given meaning. In Nehemiah 7:7, he is referred to as Raamiah, which means 'YHWH has thundered,' reflecting a theophoric element that highlights God's power. Both names identify the same individual in the post-exilic community.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Reelaiah was a descendant of Jacob, situating him within the broader covenantal lineage of Israel. Beyond this, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Reelaiah's significance lies in his role as one of the returning exiles who helped reestablish the people of Judah after the Babylonian captivity. His mention in both Ezra and Nehemiah underscores the continuity and faithfulness of God's people during the restoration period. This return was crucial for the fulfillment of God's promises to His covenant people and the reconstitution of worship and community life in Jerusalem.
